source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Enter BMC Web UI -> Click tab "Settings" ->Click tab "SSL Settings" -> Click " View CERTIFICATE MANAGEMENT" .

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.

deepseek_columns.ai_commands: curl -s -k -u "$BMC_USER:$BMC_PASS" https://$BMC_IP/redfish/v1/Managers/bmc/NetworkProtocol/HTTPS/Certificates 2>&1 | jq . 2>/dev/null; echo ---openssl---; echo | openssl s_client -connect $BMC_IP:443 -servername $BMC_IP 2>/dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -subject -issuer -dates
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: return FULL Redfish HTTPS certificate list + openssl s_client cert subject/issuer/dates so the user confirms the current certificate(s). No RISK (read-only).

It cannot prove human-readable UI rendering, complete slots/chain, SAN/hostname, fingerprint, active certificate or trust.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION / CHANGED correctly reclassifies the case because expected hostname/SAN, certificate roles, trust roots and WebUI visual correlation are material inputs, while API/TLS collection is automatable. V3.1 further defines `human readable` as labeled, untruncated, correctly formatted identity/validity/key-use/role fields and forbids private-key collection.

original_test_intent: Verify the BMC WebUI Certificate Management view opens normally and presents every in-scope certificate in a labeled, untruncated, human-readable form whose identity, role, validity and fingerprint correlate with the certificate actually served by the approved HTTPS endpoint and its trust policy.
original_method: Navigate the source Settings > SSL Settings > View Certificate Management path, capture the complete visual inventory and fields, discover/read the matching vendor certificate resources without mutation, perform a TLS handshake to the approved DNS name with verification, parse the full served chain and correlate active/stored roles, identities, fingerprints, validity and trust results while excluding private keys/secrets.
manual_activity: A human opens the source WebUI page and confirms navigation, labels, readability and absence of truncation/rendering defects. Engineering supplies expected endpoint identity, slots/roles and trust policy. Automation can retrieve/parse API and TLS evidence, but cannot substitute those for UI rendering or decide the final verdict.
required_inputs: BMC/firmware/WebUI identity and approved management DNS name/IP mapping
Expected certificate inventory: slot/role, active/inactive status, leaf/intermediate/root/CA scope
Trusted CA/reference bundle and explicit expectation for self-signed or otherwise untrusted factory certificates
Vendor certificate resource discovery and authorized read-only WebUI/API account
Human-readable UI acceptance for fields, labels, encoding, line wrapping/truncation and navigation
Metadata redaction and no-private-key evidence policy
safety_requirements: Do not clear BMC/security/audit logs or modify, generate, upload, replace, rotate or delete any certificate in this view-only case.
Never retrieve or expose private keys, account passwords, session tokens or unredacted infrastructure metadata beyond the approved evidence scope.
Do not use `curl -k` as trust validation, suppress TLS/API errors or use an IP SNI value unless that is the approved certificate identity.
Verify the exact BMC endpoint and DNS name before handshake; record certificate verification failures explicitly rather than accepting any readable certificate.
Expand the full collection and chain; distinguish stored inactive/CA material from the active served leaf and compare fingerprints.
Stop on wrong endpoint, incomplete inventory/chain, SAN mismatch, expiry/not-yet-valid state or WebUI/API/TLS disagreement; do not fix certificates in this case.
agent_execution_scope: Validate target/hostname, expected roles/identity/trust and resource schema; prepare protected read-only API/TLS collection and UI evidence checklist.
Collect complete expanded/paginated certificate inventory and a verified full-chain handshake to the approved hostname, parsing all required fields and explicit trust result.
Correlate fingerprints/roles/active state, while a human captures and evaluates the actual source WebUI navigation and readability.
Archive redacted evidence and stop without insecure trust bypass, private-key access, mutation, automated remediation or DUT verdict.
engineer_actions: Define expected endpoint/SAN, certificate roles/slots, trust roots, validity and cryptographic policy.
Perform or supervise the WebUI visual/readability checkpoint and interpret any approved factory/self-signed exception.
Review full UI/API/TLS correlation and issue the formal verdict without changing certificate state.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Only a partial hint. The generic path may not exist, collection contents are not expanded/paginated, `-k` defeats trust, credentials are exposed, IP SNI may be wrong, stderr is discarded and only one leaf's three fields are parsed. It does not exercise the source WebUI.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Discover the firmware's certificate resource and retrieve it over verified protected TLS; use `openssl s_client` or equivalent with the approved DNS SNI and CA policy to capture the full chain. Retain human WebUI inspection as a distinct checkpoint.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The exact Settings > SSL Settings > View Certificate Management path, human-readable Criteria, no Script, DeepSeek curl/jq/openssl command and 5/0-minute estimates remain preserved; Review adds no certificate write.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Correlate complete visual WebUI inventory, discovered API resources and a verified full HTTPS chain against an approved identity/trust matrix, with no certificate mutation.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: The selected BMC firmware/WebUI HTTPS certificate-management implementation and approved management DNS endpoint.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record BMC/WebUI/Redfish schema, TLS/OpenSSL client, certificate chain and trust-bundle versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: BMC vendor certificate-management schema/UI guide, Project PKI/TLS identity and cryptographic policy.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Makes `human readable` measurable and adds complete role/chain/trust correlation while preserving the source visual path.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: API/TLS automation does not prove UI layout/readability; UI content does not prove the served chain/trust; a leaf alone does not cover stored roles or intermediates.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Endpoint identity, inventory roles, trust/crypto policy, resource mapping and visual acceptance.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Read-only collection can still expose infrastructure metadata; factory self-signed certificates need explicit policy interpretation; TLS intermediaries/proxies can alter the observed chain.

project_override_considerations: A Project may use vendor API tooling for inventory and a standard TLS client for served-chain verification, but must retain the original WebUI navigation/readability checkpoint and record interface-specific coverage. API-only evidence cannot claim the UI passed; trust bypass cannot claim certificate validity.
expected_evidence: Target/firmware/WebUI identity, approved DNS/IP mapping, expected slot/role/identity/trust/crypto matrix and time reference
WebUI navigation screenshots showing complete labeled human-readable certificate fields without truncation or rendering errors
Complete expanded/paginated redacted API inventory with roles, active state, subject/SAN/issuer/serial/fingerprint/validity/key usage/algorithm
Verified full HTTPS chain for approved SNI with fingerprint correlation, hostname/SAN/validity/trust result and explicit approved exceptions
No state/private-key mutation, preserved audit evidence, interface coverage statement and engineer-owned verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure and Criteria consistently define a read-only WebUI certificate-management view and readability. The exact fields and trust expectations are under-specified but do not conflict with the purpose.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The visual certificate-inventory objective is clear. Project/vendor inputs can define expected roles, endpoint identity and trust, so missing data makes execution pending rather than permanently BLOCKED.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Changes YES to PACKAGE because expected identity/trust/schema and a human UI checkpoint are required; rejects insecure partial command as full coverage.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Agrees on hybrid classification and strengthens measurable UI readability, complete member/chain parsing and strict no-private-key scope.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.round_02: Replaces no-risk command sanity with interface/identity/trust correlation and explicit TLS failure evidence.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.related_source_cases: Keeps generate/upload/rotate operations outside this read-only verdict.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: No invalid draft exists for this exact source identity.

review_improvement: Prevents an insecure leaf-certificate dump from being reported as successful WebUI Certificate Management display and protects against silently accepting the wrong endpoint, incomplete chain or hidden UI fields.
independent_technical_reasoning: Certificate management has three distinct views: stored inventory, the active served chain and human UI rendering. Any one can disagree with the others. `human readable` requires visual field-level acceptance, while security correctness requires endpoint/SAN, fingerprints, validity and trust. Because the necessary expected identity and PKI policy are Project inputs, this is a hybrid package rather than an unconditional fully automated check.
